subject.title: [Bug] Agent context window fragmentation during concurrent subagent tool calls

question: Should concurrent child completions remain push-based in completion order with stable identifiers, or should a waiting parent receive a spawn-order batch that can block on slower earlier children?
rationale: Both behaviors are internally coherent, but spawn-order buffering changes responsiveness and failure semantics; source inspection alone cannot choose that product contract without a demonstrated mis-correlation.

options.title: Preserve completion order
options.body: Keep push-based delivery, add correlation regression coverage, and fix only any proven identifier-to-result mismatch.

options.title: Add ordered aggregation
options.body: Introduce an explicit opt-in waiting or batching primitive that releases a selected child set in spawn order without changing default completion delivery.

options.title: Make spawn order default
options.body: Buffer all concurrent completions by invocation order, accepting head-of-line blocking and delayed partial results.

recommendation.title: Preserve completion order
recommendation.body: Keep push-based delivery, add correlation regression coverage, and fix only any proven identifier-to-result mismatch.

likelyOwner.reason: The most recent identified work simplified the same subagent completion-handoff path.
